headline: Daily market snapshot November 6, 2026
summary: Pre-open snapshot for November 6, 2026. US futures mixed after Thursday's brutal tech selloff: Nasdaq 100 futures +1.35%, S&P 500 futures +0.27%, Dow futures -0.82%. Thursday closes: S&P 500 -4.36% to 7,353.73; Nasdaq -5.52% to 24,315; Dow -3.4%.

headline: 2026 midterm election results: Democrats projected to win over 250 House seats, control of Congress
summary: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the November 3, 2026 midterm elections, ending two years of unified Republican control. Democrats are projected to win over 250 House seats and Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is expected to become Speaker when the new Congress convenes in January. Major legislation will now require bipartisan negotiation.
key_facts: Democrats projected to win 250+ House seats
Jeffries expected to become House Speaker in January 2027

headline: Dow has best post-midterm elections day in 44 years as Democrats take control of Congress
summary: US stocks surged on November 4 after Democrats won the 2026 midterms and President Trump accepted the results. The Dow rose 1,569 points (3%), posting its best post-midterm election performance since 1982. The S&P 500 gained 1.58%, its second-biggest such gain in over four decades.
key_facts: Rally attributed to Trump accepting results and reduced political uncertainty

headline: Stock market today: Dow plunges 1,800 points, Nasdaq enters correction in AI trade meltdown
summary: US stocks suffered their worst single-day session in months on November 5, with the Dow dropping more than 1,800 points and the Nasdaq entering correction territory. The selloff was driven by fears that a Democratic Congress might impose tougher AI regulation and by investor concerns about whether AI infrastructure spending will ever produce adequate returns.
key_facts: ~$2.5T in market value wiped from Nasdaq alone
AI regulation fears after Democratic midterm sweep

headline: Nvidia stock plunges nearly 8% as broad AI and chip sell-off erases over 1,000 Nasdaq points
summary: Nvidia shares fell approximately 8-9% on November 5 as a broad selloff swept AI and semiconductor stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped more than 8.7% on the day, and the global chip selloff erased an estimated $500 billion in market value. AMD fell 17.26% in one of its worst single sessions.
key_facts: ~$500B in global chip market cap erased
Largest Nasdaq single-day drop in 19 months

headline: Nasdaq futures rise after steep AI selloff as chip stocks stabilize

Drivers: AI regulation fears, ROI doubts, debt concerns

key_facts: APP +31% intraday Nov 5, top S&P 500 gainer

headline: Palantir Q3 2026: US commercial revenue +148% YoY, total revenue +96% YoY; raises FY 2026 guidance to 91% growth
summary: Palantir reported Q3 2026 results on November 2, massively beating expectations with total revenue of $2.313 billion, up 96% year over year. EPS of $0.44 beat the $0.41 consensus. headline: Marvell agrees to $115B all-stock deal for Lumentum, biggest public-tech M&A ever
summary: Marvell Technology announced it will acquire Lumentum Holdings in a $115 billion all-stock deal, described as the largest equity-value technology M&A transaction ever. Lumentum shareholders receive 4.5 Marvell shares per share, a ~23.9% premium to the October 28 close. Marvell shareholders would own approximately 67% of the combined company upon closing, expected in the first half of 2028.
key_facts: All-stock deal valued at $115B enterprise value
Marvell shareholders ~67%, Lumentum ~33% of combined company
3 Lumentum board members including CEO join Marvell board
Expected close H1 2028, pending regulatory and shareholder approval

summary: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4.00% at its October 2026 meeting, following a 25-basis-point hike in September 2026, the first increase since 2023. ADP showed private payrolls +86,000 in October. Average payroll growth since January 2025 has been only ~35,000 per month.

The 10-year yield dropped to approximately 4.85%, and the 2-year fell to around 4.48-4.50%, with the 2-year declining faster than the 10-year as traders scaled back wagers on aggressive rate hikes. The yield curve remains positively sloped at about 30-35 basis points.
